story_text.value:
I’m writing my first novel and could not find an app that fit my workflow: quiet like iA Writer, organized like Scrivener, and with AI so I can discuss my book while I write it. It allows me to feel less “alone” and have a sounding board while I write.

- A book is a folder of plain Markdown files. Musset commits to a git repo, tracks versions and drafts without you having to know git.

- Revisions are CriticMarkup inside the text. It manages docx revisions too, so your editor can edit a Word doc and you import their comments.

- PDFs are typeset using Typst, embedded in the app, following each language’s typographic rules.

- Spelling and grammar are checked using LanguageTool, also embedded.

- Mac/Word, WordStar, vi and Emacs keyboard modes.

The AI is optional and uses your Codex or Claude Code CLI. It comments, leaves margin notes, and checks continuity and your chapters against your style rules.

It’s GPL-3.0 and free during the beta. When or if it reaches 1.0, if there is sufficient interest, the idea is to make it a small one-time payment ($9.90). There is a paid sync service (git hosting) that lets you share a book with beta readers and editors.

Download: https://musset.app

I’d love to have some feedback!

title.value: Show HN: Musset, open-source Scrivener alternative with an AI that never writes

story_text.value: Hi HN. I’m Ed. I built MuGlobe solo. It’s a global music discovery platform. Click on any spot on the globe and stream music from there. It’s not playlists stuck to a globe. It’s a huge ethnomusicology database that paints > 1500 musical genres onto the world then maps the overlapping influences into a virtual radio station that then generates a dynamic list from 100,000 cataloged tracks on Youtube. It’s free and has no ads. I want it to be used to cure the music algorithm blues. Do you think its a fit or that use case or better in education?  I find a lot of the music in Latin America and Africa can be left on all day.

story_text.value:
A personal project for digging deeper into Linux system programming, ObFUSEcate implements a file backed virtual block device that automatically performs compression and encryption as blocks are accessed. This virtual device can be mounted via FUSE (requiring no root privileges) to provide, effectively, a "live" compressed, encrypted archive.

Written in C++, and intended to have minimal dependencies, it has custom 32 bit arithmetic encoding/decoding, ChaCha20-Poly1305 authenticated encryption, and CRC8 + XOR parity error-correction.

title.value: Show HN: Lightweight FUSE-based encrypted, compressed filesystem for Linux

story_text.value:
I've been working on this country naming/geography game on and off over the past few months but most of it in Oct/Nov, using only free tier Claude (Sonnet 5 and 5.5)

It started off as just wanting to make a fun little thing for myself that included features in this sort of game that I couldn't find on existing sites. As I went on with it adding more stuff and ideas from friends it also turned into sorta like proving to myself that Sonnet and the free tier restrictions were still good enough to work on fun little things like this.

Happy to get any sort of feedback anyone is interested in giving. It does work on both mobile and desktop, and you get a little sharable results image when you're done. You can combine any of the different modes together or just play in normal mode.

story_text.value:
Hi HN,

I wanted a PDF viewer I could drive entirely from the keyboard that could also fill in forms and sign documents.

You might already be acquainted with PDF viewers like zathura and sioyek. This one is similar, except much more performant and not prone to crashes. You can also draw, annotate and fill & sign entirely via keyboard.

It's based off of PdfCraft's (from the ArtCraft project) rendering engine.

The config is configured in TOML and live-reloaded.

Feel free to try and give feedback.

story_text.value:
Hey HN, I have build a tool after my own job searching. You describe the job you want in a sentence, like "backend roles in Zurich, Python, no banks", and it searches the web and companies' own career pages for it. There is no bias, no curated lists, no promotion; only a pure and powerful search.

I wanted to get the real postings. The same jobs can show up to many boards and recruiter sites, often after it's closed. Don't you want to know this? Craoli tries to find the employer's own postings, shows one card for all the copies that exist out there, and keeps checking whether the job is still open.

Another issue I had was that one company while I submitted my job application, changed the job description, by adding one more requirement that was not there when I have applied!! Good luck proving that. Of course the recruiter brought this point for my rejection, that I was sure that it was not there when I applied. 7+ years of pre-sales is hard to miss on a job description when read.

There are some limits for now; career pages are read directly only for the common hiring systems; a custom site is only found through web search. And every search costs me real money, so you need an account, and free has 2 searches a month using a cheaper LLM model; the search costs the same. Additional classical features are there for you to discover, like tailored CVs and cover letters.

What I would like to know: the last time you looked for a job, what made you stop trusting a listing?

title.value: Show HN: Craoli – describe a job in one sentence, it finds real postings
